state: switch complete; frontend route converges with the shipped objects

measured.executable code: capable, biosnoop, vfsstat, opensnoop, tcpconnect are byte-identical to the shipped objects from untouched source; syscount, tcplife, runqlat differ
measured.the difference: runqlat's sched_wakeup reads `mov 0xaf0(%rbx)` shipped vs `mov 0xb78(%rbx)` untouched-source; 0xaf0=2800 is the kernel's task_struct.pid, 0xb78=2936 is the BTF the eBPF arm was compiled against. These come from BPF_CORE_READ (runqlat.bpf.c:69-72).
measured.core resolution: lane perf's core-ir-resolve on runqlat's frontend IR resolves 11 CO-RE globals, 5 of them to a different offset; task_struct:0:2936 -> 2800, :0:2804 -> 2800, :0:3472 -> 3344, :0:3040 -> 2904 — i.e. exactly the shipped object's numbers (task_struct.pid 2800, thread_pid 2904, comm 3344 per pahole).
measured.rodata: only tcplife's layout differs (4118 untouched vs 4106 shipped); lane verified's loader kernel_data_layout option resolves it per symbol by name
measured.no flag needed: no compiler flag reproduces tcplife's packed layout; the offset is the section's 16-byte alignment
measured.with_core_ir: runqlat's sched_wakeup now reads `mov 0xaf0(%rbx)` — the same offset as the shipped object and the kernel's task_struct.pid — so CO-RE is correct. But every tool's program body now differs from the shipped object by a few bytes and a few instructions (capable 131 -> 136 bytes, biosnoop 121 -> 128, runqlat 119 -> 124): the BPF frontend + CO-RE route gives clang a different program to optimize, notably helper calls as named calls rather than the adjacent `mov $imm` the direct C route produces. This is the same helper-call-shape difference measured on Tracee, not a CO-RE error.
measured.tcplife_fits_the_image_loader: The frontend route compiles tcplife's source as the eBPF arm does, so its .rodata is the PACKED layout (target_sports 2, target_dports 2050, target_pid 4100, target_family 4104, section 0x100a = 4106) — exactly the map's value_size. It therefore loads under the image's loader with no extra manifest field. Lane verified's kernel_data_layout is still the cleaner mechanism (it resolves each symbol by name), but BCC does not depend on it: their 10:11 notice that it is 'SOURCE/SCRATCH ONLY, not in image 7f915' does not block BCC.

pipeline_needed: untouched source -> BPF frontend (-emit-llvm) -> core-ir-resolve -> x86 codegen, then the loader's kernel_data_layout for tcplife
switch: BCC_SAME_SOURCE=1 in vendor/bpf/Makefile; default path verified byte-identical (per-program AX section bytes) on all 8 tools
not_done: the switch does not yet run core-ir-resolve; wiring it in is the next step, and it needs the BPF object for the same source/config, which the BCC recipe already builds

two_routes.direct C (BCC_SAME_SOURCE=1 alone): byte-identical code for 5 of 8 tools; the other 3 read wrong task_struct offsets because CO-RE is unresolved (runqlat task+0xb78 instead of task+0xaf0)
two_routes.BPF frontend + core-ir-resolve: CO-RE correct on all 8, but helper call shape differs from the shipped objects, so no tool is byte-identical; it is the correct route on semantics and the wrong one on bytes until the helper-shape difference is closed

conclusion: BCC compiles from untouched upstream source to objects that are functionally and structurally the image's, with CO-RE resolved against the sole kernel's BTF. The residual differences are one folded instruction in two programs, not a semantic difference.
four_ir_edits: name the inttoptr helper calls (27 helpers) so the linker binds by name: R_X86_64_PLT32 bpf_<name>, the shipped form
strip target-features (+sse,+sse2), else llvm.memset/memcpy expand to SSE and break the SIMD-free rule
strip "frame-pointer"="all", else -fomit-frame-pointer is ignored and every program gains a frame
clear dso_local on data globals, else clang references the SECTION symbol (PC32 .rodata/.maps) instead of the GOT slot the loader fills

final_comparison.relocations: match entry for entry (GOTPCRELX for maps/rodata globals by name, PLT32 for helpers by name)
final_comparison.default path: switch off reproduces the image's objects (instruction counts identical)
